name: Cornwall and West Devon Mining Landscape
countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: Across Cornwall and West Devon in south-west England, the ruined stone engine houses of old tin and copper mines still stand on cliffs, moors and hillsides. In the early 19th century this region supplied two-thirds of the world's copper. Its steam-engine technology was exported worldwide. Alongside the mines you can see foundries, harbours, miners' smallholdings and the towns that grew around them.
